parts:
I created a StackOverflow post about creating a dynamic number of inputSlider object when the number required is not known in advance:
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19130455/create-dynamic-number-of-input-elements-with-r-shiny

I got great advice and attempted to implement it. The full post is there, but the summary is that I'm doing the following:

ui.R
----------
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  headerPanel("Side by side comparison"),
  
  sidebarPanel(
        
    sliderInput(inputId = "members", label = "Number of individuals on plan:",
                min = 1, max = 15, value = 2, step = 1),
      
    sliderInput(inputId = "max_pred", label = "Maximum for expense range:",
                min = 5000, max = 100000, value = 5000, step = 5000),
    
    uiOutput("sliders")

    ),
  
  mainPanel(
      plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot", width = "100%"))
)))


server.R
----------
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  
  output$sliders <- renderUI({
    members <- as.integer(input$members)
    max_pred <- as.integer(input$max_pred)
    lapply(1:members, function(i) {
      sliderInput(inputId = paste0("ind", i), label = paste("Individual", i),
                  min = 0, max = max_pred, value = c(0, 500), step = 100)
    })
    
  })
  
  expenses <- reactive({
    print(names(input))
    members <- as.numeric(input$members)
    
    mins <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[1]
    })
    
    maxs <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[2]
    })
    
    expenses <- as.data.frame(cbind(mins, maxs))
  })

  best_case <- reactive({
    
    expenses <- expenses()
    ...
    ...
  })

That's enough to explain the problem. I got errors about applying a non-function and started digging around a bit. I used browser() inside the expenses <- reactive({}) bit above and was perplexed by the fact that ls() didn't show an input or output object existing. I tried putting print(names(input)) at the top of it, and got *two* print-outs in the session window:
[1] "class"    "max_pred" "members" 
[1] "class"    "ind1"     "ind2"     "max_pred" "members"

I did the same for print(expenses) and also got two:
# the first
  mins maxs
1   NA   NA
2   NA   NA

# the second
  mins maxs
1    0  500
2    0  500

So, it's making me think something's goofy about my expenses definition, or that somehow the outputUI bit hasn't done it's thing by the time expenses is run, but *does* get run when I run the line `expenses <- expenses()` and re-call it.

Any suggestions? I have no idea how to troubleshoot this one!



Thanks,
John

To help you debug and understand your dependencies, simply put options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE); after library(shiny) in your server.R code and press Ctrl+F3 in your browser and see.

Also the code re-uses the name expenses in a few instances. Not sure if it's a problem but to avoid confusion may I suggest you use different names. E.g. you have expenses <- expenses(), why not just expenses_result <- expenses().

I believe ls() show you only the objects that exists in the current environment, so ls() won't show you input output.

I suspect there is nothing goofy about the double print. When shiny starts everything is run once to help it determine the dependencies. The first time it runs input$members is null so it prints the first time. Then I suppose some where in your code input$members is updated which causes expenses to run a second time. Try this to see if it explains.

expenses <- reactive({
    print(names(input))
    members <- as.numeric(input$members)
    
    mins <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[1]
    })
    
    maxs <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[2]
    })

expenses_result <- as.data.frame(cbind(mins, maxs))
    print("Finished running once")
    expenses_result

  })
